gap: No result ChatGPT got works out, product by product, how many screens actually run with no driver: the lowest of three numbers, which are the screens in the box, the laptop's video-capable USB-C ports and the laptop's own external-display limit. For the Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro that is min(2, 2, 2) = 2 on a Mac with two DisplayPort USB-C ports, but min(2, 2, 1) = 1 on a plain M1 or M2 MacBook, where Macworld says the second screen needs Mobile Pixels' DisplayLink-like software.
standout_why: I compared against these pages. deskgearhq.com (2026-07-26, opened) lists the Trio 3 Pro as 'No driver required' with 'Single USB-C cable drives both panels', and it gives no weight, wattage or port count for any pick. Macworld says the opposite: two USB-C cables, and software on single-display Macs. ChatGPT's own answer gives only the general rule (base M-series Macs drive one external display) and never applies it to a specific product. I could not open the cited FOPO S11 and Plugable pages, the Best Buy UPERFECT page or the tutt.ca S10 page: the first three returned HTTP 429 or timed out, and tutt.ca returned 429. gradedpicks.com failed its TLS check. So I can't rule out that one of those pages states a per-product port count. That is why I score this 2 and not 3.
decides: It confirms that the first pick follows the laptop, not the screen. A two-screen extender is driver-free only when the laptop has two video-capable USB-C ports and drives two external displays. On a plain M1 or M2 MacBook (Macworld names them), the Trio 3 Pro gets one screen without software, so a single-screen model is the honest driver-free pick for that shopper. The Duex Float 2 Pro needs one DP Alt Mode port for its one screen (7.5 W typical, 2.9 lb), and Duex Max DS is our other single-screen row. Dual extenders such as FOPO S1, S7 and S11 and the Trio 3 Pro win for Windows laptops and Pro/Max MacBooks that have two video-capable ports. It also rules out the FOPO S788 for this question: our record says it requires the UsbDisplay driver.

findings.label: Screens that run driver-free
findings.value: 2 on a laptop with two DisplayPort-enabled USB-C ports; 1 on a plain M1 or M2 MacBook (the second screen needs Mobile Pixels' software)
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review (Simon Jary, Macworld, Apr 2, 2026)
findings.note: min(screens 2, video USB-C ports 2, Mac display limit 1) = 1 on plain M1/M2. Macworld: 'The screens connect to the MacBook with the included two USB-C cables'; Macs with two DisplayPort-enabled USB-C ports need no software; plain M1 and M2 Macs and the MacBook Neo are limited to one monitor and must 'download and install free software (rather like DisplayLink)'. One sentence in the review says base M1, M2 and M3 can drive both screens, which contradicts the line before it, so I used only the explicit M1/M2 statement.
